newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf signs oil exploration deal with Azerbaijan.
newsitem.headline: Elf signs oil exploration deal with Azerbaijan.

text.p: French oil group Elf Aquitaine said on Monday it had signed a production sharing contract covering the off-shore Lenkoran-Talysh Deniz permit with Azerbaijan's Socar.
The contract was signed in the presence of Azeri President Geidar Aleyev, on a three-day visit in France, and President Jacques Chirac.

Elf will take an initial 65 percent stake as operator in the field, while state oil group Socar will have a 25 percent stake. French oil group Total SA has 10 percent and there are negotiations underway for other companies to join the consortium.
A spokesman for Elf declined to detail the estimated reserves nor the investments needed.

The Lenkoran-Talysh Deniz project calls for exploration and production within an area of 420 square kilometres in the Caspian Sea, 300 kilometres south of Baku, in water depths ranging from 20 to 100 metres.
The contract covers a period of 30 years.
